climbs.name: Puerto de El Duque
notes: Never before climbed in Vuelta history. Ascends the same Genil River valley as Alto de Hazallanas, with an identical final 2km finishing on the same road to the Sierra Nevada ski resort — but shorter and slightly easier, and without the 18-19% ramps that mark Hazallanas' opening kilometres after the technical descent from Güéjar Sierra. Length/gradient from our own GPX route data (previously an estimate of 4.8km/8.2% — the real climb is closer to twice that length, following on from Puerto de El Purche in the stage's own sequencing).

climbs.name: Puerto de El Miserat
notes: A genuinely steep climb, not the gentle grind the old figure suggested — checked against the official stage profile chart, which places the categorised col right after Pego. Confirmed geographically: the true start (matching the site's own GPX data) reverse-geocodes exactly to Pego. Length/gradient from our own GPX route data (previously a mistaken 18km/2.6% — Cat1 here really does reflect steepness, with ramps over 20%).
